questions.question:
**Select the correct indirect form of the given sentence.**

Aanya said to, "I've made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for you."

options.text: Aanya told me that she had made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.
Aanya told me that she is making a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.
Aanya tell me that she would make a rose and honey vanilla dessert for her.
Aanya said to me that she was making a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'Aanya told me that he had made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence is in **Direct Narration.** As per the given question we have to change it into **Indirect Narration. **
 
• The process of transformation as follows: 
 
 
• **'Said to' **will be changed into **'told'.** Though** the reporting verb has no object, it is understood. **
 
• **Comma and inverted comma will be removed. **
 
• **'I' **will be changed into **'She'. **
 
• **'Have made'** will be changed into **'had made'. **
 
• **'You' **will be changed into **'me'. **
 
 
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence will be **'Aanya told me that she had made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me.'**

 

**Correct Answer:__** *Aanya told me that she had made a rose and honey vanilla dessert for me. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select ‘No improvement’.**

Doctors at the AIIMS Trauma Centre managed to save the life of 12-year-old archer Shivangini, __whose were struck__ by an arrow in the neck during a practice session.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'who was struck'. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The given sentence requires improvement. 
 
• **'whose were struck'** should be changed into **'who was struck'. **
 
• **'Who'** is a **relative pronoun.** **'Whose'** is used for the plural subject. Whereas, **'who' **should be used. 
 
• **We know that relative pronouns are used as a subject of a subordinate clause. **
 
• In the given sentence subject **'Shivangini'** is a singular subject.
 
• Therefore, a singular form of the verb** 'was' **should be used. 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is** 'who was struck'. **

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *Doctors at the AIIMS Trauma Centre managed to save the life of 12-year-old archer Shivangini, **who was struck** by an arrow in the neck during a practice session. *

questions.question:
**In the given sentence, identify the segment which contains the grammatical error.**

The performance of our players is worst than I had expected.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'worst than'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The erroneous Part** 'worst than' should have 'worse than' instead. **
 
• We know that** ''than'' **is used with the comparative and** 'of' and 'among' **is used superlative degree. 
 
• Here, in the given sentence** 'worst' **is the superlative degree of **'bad'. **
 
• Whereas, the given sentence needs a comparative degree of **'bad'** that is** 'worse'. **
 
• Therefore, **Option 3** is the correct answer.

 

**Correct Sentence:__** *The performance of our players is **worse than** I had expected. *

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• We should avoid using double comparatives and superlatives in a sentence together. 
 
 
• *Alexander was **more taller** than John. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b91b169c9a6aba309887b5e1410c56688829831001bc1448ed23f1bec5eca1d8.png] *

questions.question:
**Given below are four jumbled sentences. Pick the option that gives their correct order.**

A. When we wish to achieve something, we cannot expect success in a moment.

B. It is the same with any great achievement.

C. It took several years to build Rome and bring it to the state of glory.

D. Rome, the greatest city of the ancient world was not built in a short time.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'DCBA'.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Only **Part D** can be the first sentence because the first statement of a para jumble question is usually **a general statement, noun, most, once, a universal fact, or starting of an incident, etc. **
 
• In the given question only **Part D** starts with a **Noun** that is **Rome**. It is also **a general statement. **
 
• Part C should be the next sentence because it explains **Part D. **
 
• Therefore, Part C and Part D make a pair. And only **Option 4** starts with **Part D** and **Part D** should be followed by **Part C.**
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **DCBA. **

**​**

**Correct Answer:__** *DCBA.*
